title: Extension of a partially multiplicative SL2 open-cell map to a group sheaf
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$, with multiplication, inverse and identity obeying the group identities; it is separated when its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On $S$-schemes use the fppf topology, whose covering families are jointly surjective flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. Write $\mathbf G_a(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ with addition and $\mathbf G_m(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$ with multiplication, for every $S$-scheme $T$. A group sheaf means a group-valued functor with unique gluing of compatible sections for these coverings. A central exact sequence means that its first map identifies its source with the kernel of its second map, the second map is locally surjective for this topology, and the kernel commutes with every local section of the middle sheaf. Write $G=\operatorname{SL}_{2,S}$ for the group sheaf of determinant-one $2\times2$ matrices of global functions, and put $x(u)=I_2+uE_{12}$, $y(v)=I_2+vE_{21}$, where $I_2$ is the identity matrix and $E_{ij}$ has entry $1$ at $(i,j)$ and zero elsewhere, and $h(t)=\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})$. Let $\Omega\subseteq G$ be the subfunctor where the bottom-right matrix entry is invertible; it is represented by the open subscheme of $G$ with that condition. Its coordinates are $x(u)h(t)y(v)$, with $u,v\in\mathbf G_a$ and $t\in\mathbf G_m$. Let $H$ be any group sheaf, with no representability or separatedness hypothesis, and let $\sigma:\Omega\to H$ be a natural transformation such that $\sigma(1)=1$ and $\sigma(a)\sigma(b)=\sigma(ab)$ for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every $a,b\in\Omega(T)$ with $ab\in\Omega(T)$. There exists a unique homomorphism of group sheaves $\widetilde\sigma:G\to H$ whose restriction to $\Omega$ is $\sigma$.

proof.text: For finitely many $g_i=(g_{i,jk})_{1\leq j,k\leq2},\quad (a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i)=(g_{i,11},g_{i,12},g_{i,21},g_{i,22})\in G(T)$, cover $T$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The determinant equation gives $(-c_i)b_i+a_i d_i=1$. Apply [lem-sfb-unimodular-linear-forms-fppf-cover] to obtain an fppf covering and $z$ with all $b_i z+d_i$ invertible. Set $\omega=y(z)$. Both $\omega$ and $\omega^{-1}=y(-z)$ lie in $\Omega$, and the bottom-right entry of $\omega g_i$ is $b_i z+d_i$. Hence $\omega g_i\in\Omega$ for every $i$. In particular, with just $g$ we get the local word $g=\omega^{-1}(\omega g)$ of two elements of $\Omega$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 4.3.1, printed pp.130--131, finite-word comparison (4.3.2); read online 2026-10-24, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Compare any two finite words $a_1\cdots a_n=b_1\cdots b_m=g$ with all letters in $\Omega(T)$, allowing an empty word. Apply step 1 simultaneously to their finitely many nonempty prefix products and obtain $\omega\in\Omega$ such that every translated prefix lies in $\Omega$. For prefixes $A_i=a_1\cdots a_i$ put $A_0=1$. Induction from $i=0$ using the hypothesis on $\sigma$ for $(\omega A_{i-1},a_i)$ gives $\sigma(\omega A_i)=\sigma(\omega)\sigma(a_1)\cdots\sigma(a_i)$. The same induction for the $b$-word gives $\sigma(\omega g)=\sigma(\omega)\sigma(b_1)\cdots\sigma(b_m)$. Cancel $\sigma(\omega)$ on the left in $H$. Equality holds before the covering because $H$ has unique gluing. Thus every pair of equal $\Omega$-words has equal products of its $\sigma$-values.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 4.3.1, printed pp.130--131, finite-word comparison (4.3.2); read online 2026-10-24, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $g\in G(T)$ choose the local two-letter words supplied by step 1 and take the product of their $\sigma$-values. On a pairwise overlap the words have the same product in $G$, so step 2 makes their values equal in $H$. The sheaf axiom for $H$ glues them uniquely to $\widetilde\sigma_T(g)\in H(T)$. Any other choice agrees on the common covering by pairwise fibre products, again by step 2, and hence gives the same section. For $T'\to T$, pull back the chosen covering and its words; naturality of $\sigma$ identifies their values with the restrictions of the old values. Uniqueness of gluing proves naturality of $\widetilde\sigma$. If $g\in\Omega(T)$ compare with the one-letter word $(g)$ in step 2 to obtain $\widetilde\sigma_T(g)=\sigma_T(g)$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 4.3.1, printed pp.130--131, finite-word comparison (4.3.2); read online 2026-10-24, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $g,h\in G(T)$ take a common refinement of coverings with $\Omega$-words for $g$ and $h$. Their concatenation is an $\Omega$-word for $gh$. Step 2 compares it with a chosen local word for $gh$, so $\widetilde\sigma(gh)=\widetilde\sigma(g)\widetilde\sigma(h)$ locally and then in $H(T)$ by unique gluing. The empty word and $\sigma(1)=1$ give $\widetilde\sigma(1)=1$; applying the product identity to $g,g^{-1}$ gives preservation of inverses. Finally, any homomorphism extending $\sigma$ takes each local $\Omega$-word to this same product. Unique gluing therefore makes it equal to $\widetilde\sigma$ on every $T$.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_sl2_openCell_extension (S : Scheme.{u}) (H : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) GrpCat.{v}) (σ : ∀ (T : Over S) (g : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) Γ(T.left, ⊤)), IsUnit (g 1 1) → H.obj.obj (op T)) (hσ_natural : ∀ (T U : Over S) (f : U ⟶ T) (g : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) Γ(T.left, ⊤)) (hg : IsUnit (g 1 1)), H.obj.map f.op (σ T g hg) = σ U (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map f.left.appTop.hom g) (hg.map f.left.appTop.hom)) (hσ_one : ∀ T : Over S, σ T 1 isUnit_one = 1) (hσ_mul : ∀ (T : Over S) (a b : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) Γ(T.left, ⊤)) (ha : IsUnit (a 1 1)) (hb : IsUnit (b 1 1)) (hab : IsUnit ((a * b) 1 1)), σ T a ha * σ T b hb = σ T (a * b) hab) : ∃! τ : ∀ T : Over S, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) Γ(T.left, ⊤) →* H.obj.obj (op T), (∀ (T U : Over S) (f : U ⟶ T) (g : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) Γ(T.left, ⊤)), H.obj.map f.op (τ T g) = τ U (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map f.left.appTop.hom g)) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (g : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) Γ(T.left, ⊤)) (hg : IsUnit (g 1 1)), τ T g = σ T g hg)
lean.note: The open cell is expressed by IsUnit (g 1 1) on the existing Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup of global sections. Natural maps and natural group homomorphisms are written componentwise; no second SL2 or open-cell definition and no representability hypothesis on H are introduced.
